_about: Pairs are checked only between ingredients from DIFFERENT brands (e.g. Telma-AM alone never warns about its own telmisartan + amlodipine). Levels: warning = do not combine unless a doctor says so; caution = tell your doctor or pharmacist you take both; timing = can be taken, but not at the same time. Every pair is taken from a line on the listed source page(s).

same_ingredient.message: Both medicines contain {ingredient}. Taking them together could mean taking too much. Ask your doctor or pharmacist before taking both.

same_class.message: Both medicines are the same type of medicine ({class}). Ask your doctor or pharmacist whether you should take both.

pairs.message: Ibuprofen and diclofenac are both NSAID painkillers. Taking them together raises the risk of side effects like stomach ulcers. Do not take both unless a doctor says so.
Ibuprofen and aspirin are both NSAIDs. Taking them together raises the risk of serious side effects like stomach ulcers. Do not take both unless a doctor says so.
Diclofenac and aspirin are both NSAIDs. Taking them together raises the risk of side effects like stomach problems. Do not take both without talking to a doctor.
Azithromycin and domperidone can both affect your heartbeat. Tell your doctor before taking them together.
NSAID painkillers like ibuprofen can affect telmisartan. Do not start ibuprofen without asking your doctor.
NSAID painkillers like diclofenac can affect telmisartan. Do not start diclofenac without asking your doctor.
Aspirin may interact with telmisartan. Make sure your doctor knows you take both.
These are two blood pressure medicines. Make sure your doctor knows you take both.
Ibuprofen may not mix well with blood pressure medicines like amlodipine. Check with your pharmacist or doctor.
Diclofenac may not mix well with blood pressure medicines like amlodipine. Check with your doctor or pharmacist.
Aspirin may not mix well with some blood pressure medicines. Make sure your doctor knows you take both.
NSAID painkillers like ibuprofen may interact with glimepiride. Do not start ibuprofen without asking your doctor.
NSAID painkillers like diclofenac may interact with glimepiride. Do not start diclofenac without asking your doctor.
Aspirin may interact with glimepiride. Make sure your doctor knows you take both.
NSAID painkillers like ibuprofen may not mix well with metformin. Tell your doctor or pharmacist you take both.
NSAID painkillers like diclofenac may not mix well with metformin. Tell your doctor or pharmacist you take both.
Calcium can stop levothyroxine working as well. Do not take them at the same time - ask your pharmacist how far apart to take them.
Stomach acid medicines like omeprazole may not mix well with levothyroxine. Tell your doctor you take both.
Stomach acid medicines like esomeprazole may not mix well with levothyroxine. Tell your doctor you take both.
Stomach acid medicines like pantoprazole may not mix well with levothyroxine. Tell your doctor you take both.
Stomach acid medicines like famotidine may not mix well with levothyroxine. Tell your doctor you take both.
Famotidine and omeprazole both reduce stomach acid. Do not take both unless your doctor agrees.
Famotidine and esomeprazole are both heartburn medicines. Do not take both unless your doctor agrees.
Famotidine and pantoprazole are both heartburn medicines. Do not take both unless your doctor agrees.
Azithromycin may not mix well with statins like atorvastatin. Tell your doctor before taking them together.
Some antibiotics can affect domperidone. Tell your doctor or pharmacist you take both.
Domperidone may not mix well with heart or blood pressure medicines. Tell your doctor or pharmacist you take both.
Domperidone may not mix well with heart or blood pressure medicines. Tell your doctor or pharmacist you take both.
Anti-sickness medicines like domperidone may not mix well with paracetamol. Check with your pharmacist.
Cetirizine and levocetirizine are very similar allergy medicines and both can make you sleepy. Ask your pharmacist before taking both.
Both can make you drowsy. Taking them together may make you sleepier. Check with your pharmacist and do not drive if you feel sleepy.
Both can make you drowsy. Taking them together may make you sleepier. Check with your pharmacist and do not drive if you feel sleepy.
Do not take extra calcium or vitamin D supplements together unless your doctor agrees - too much calcium can be harmful.
